state.task: Two agents analysed Java code for path traversal (CWE-22). Their final answers follow, then the code of each method in question.
agent_answers: {"findings": [{"cwe": "CWE-22", "class": "InputStreamHelper", "method": "processZipStream", "explanation": "The zip entry name obtained from ZipEntry.getName() is used directly as the file path when creating a new File object with new File(dir, entry.getName()), bypassing any path normalization or validation that would prevent directory traversal attacks, allowing an attacker to write files outside the intended temporary directory."}]}

{"findings": [{"cwe": "CWE-22", "class": "InputStreamHelper", "method": "processZipStream", "explanation": "The method processZipStream uses ZipEntry.getName() (a tainted source) to construct a File object via new File(dir, entry.getName()) and then opens a FileOutputStream on that file, without validating that the entry name does not contain path traversal sequences (e.g., \"../\"). This allows an attacker to write files outside the intended temporary directory, leading to a Zip Slip vulnerability."}]}

m1.instructions: True if the agents' final answers conclude that the method InputStreamHelper.processZipStream is part of a path traversal vulnerability (it builds, passes or opens the attacker-controlled path).
